name: Agreement with the Indians of the Blackfeet Agency, 1887 (ratified by the Act of May 1, 1888)
nations: Amskapi Piikani (Blackfeet Nation; Piegan, Blood and Blackfeet bands)
promises: Article I and the Blackfeet Agency boundary clause signed February 11, 1887: the Piegan, Blood and Blackfeet bands kept a separate reservation (the present Blackfeet Reservation, bounded by the Marias River, Cut Bank Creek, the northern boundary of Montana, the Rocky Mountains and Birch Creek); under Article II they gave up their rights in the rest of the joint reservation.
Article III: $150,000 a year for ten years for the Blackfeet agency, spent on cattle, goods, clothing, food, tools, schooling, medical care and care of the aged and orphans.
Article IV: any yearly surplus to be held in the Treasury for the bands and spent after the ten years ran out.
Article VI: any member already settled on ceded land could have it allotted to the family.

breaches.what: The Indian Claims Commission found that the 14,969,156 acres ceded under the 1886-87 agreements, ratified May 1, 1888, were worth $11,975,324.80 (80 cents an acre) and that the $4,300,000 promised was unconscionable on its face. It made interlocutory awards to the Blackfeet Nation, the Assiniboine and the Fort Peck Sioux.

breaches.quote: an agreed consideration of $4,300,000 for lands having a value of $11,975,324.80 as of the date of taking is unconscionable on its face

landTaken: The agreements ceded the great joint reservation of the Gros Ventre, Piegan, Blood, Blackfeet and River Crow in northern Montana, except three separate reservations; the ICC put the ceded area at 14,969,156 acres (Docket 279-A findings, 1967).
compensation: Article III of the agreement ratified by the 1888 Act promised, for ten years, $165,000 a year for the Fort Peck agency, $115,000 for Fort Belknap and $150,000 for Blackfeet (25 Stat. 113); the Commission gives the agreed consideration as $4,300,000 (Docket 279-A, 1967). After the 1967 liability finding, the Commission entered final judgments in 1968: $8,679,814.92 to the Blackfeet and Gros Ventre Tribes and $1,161,354.41 to the Fort Peck Sioux, both by compromise of the consideration and offset issues only, and $3,108,506.40 to the Assiniboine of Fort Belknap and Fort Peck, after finding their 1888 payments had already been credited against an earlier Court of Claims award (77 C. Cls. 347).
today: The Blackfeet Nation shared in the $8,679,814.92 final judgment of 1968 (Docket 279-A).

nationVoice.summary: The Nation's own history says that after Lame Bull's Treaty of 1855 more treaties and agreements followed, each taking huge parts of its land, negotiated when it was not equipped to negotiate or even understand them and while the Starvation Winter of the 1880s cut its people to perhaps fewer than 3,000, and that it kept its present reservation only because it was the land the United States wanted least.

openQuestions: No Blackfeet Nation page on the 1887 agreement could be opened (blackfeetnation.com/history/ returned nothing on 2026-11-07).
Royce's three 1888 cessions (692, 693 and 695) are parts of the one 14,969,156-acre area the ICC valued as a unit; the ICC did not value each agency's part separately.
The 1888 consideration was not cash to the nations but goods, stock, schooling and agency expenses spent at the Secretary's direction; whether the full ten instalments were spent was not checked.
Lead: a later cession of the Rocky Mountain part of the Blackfeet Reservation (1895-96, per the researcher) needs its own primary source.

Audit 2026-11-08: Removed 'about 29 cents an acre' from the breach: a figure the researcher computed, not one the Commission states. First promise re-cited: the separate reservation is set by Article I and the agency's boundary clause, not Article II, which is the cession. Compensation: the $4,300,000 total is the Commission's figure; the Act itself gives only the annual amounts per agency. Removed from 'today' an unsourced later cession; kept as a lead in openQuestions.
